new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (no catalog record, no statement held by the project; every source read so far — Trail 1970, Boopathy 1974, Grierson 1907, Shantha Naik 2023 — was silent on stress). First explicit statement for the language: stress non-phonemic, sentence-level only; it gives no word-level placement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only stress statement in the thesis: stress is non-phonemic in Bastar Banjari and is treated as a sentence-level phenomenon; the suprasegmental phonemes set up (1.9.6.2, pp. 44-46) are nasalization, juncture /+/ and three terminal contours, with no word-stress phoneme and no rule for where stress falls in the word. (Verified against the page scan; the scanned text garbles the passage.)
new_statements.exceptions: none; the lexicon (Part four) labels a few items 'stressed form of' / 'unstressed form of' (e.g. ti:n 'stressed form of tin three', tu: 'stressed form of tu you') and lists two 'stress particle' entries (to, hi), i.e. emphatic variants, not word-stress placement
new_statements.identity_note: Singh 1976 describes the Banjari of Bastar district (Jagdalpur, Kondagaon, Bijapur and Konta tahsils; then Madhya Pradesh, now Chhattisgarh), an eastern outlier of Lambadi/Banjari; Tabassum 2019 describes Lambani of north-east Karnataka (informants from Gulbarga/Kalaburagi, Yadgir, Raichur and Bidar districts), i.e. the same region as Trail 1970 (Gulbarga). Both fall under glottocode lamb1269.

tone.quote: काही भाषांमध्ये आरोह - अवरोह किंवा विशिष्ट प्रकारचे हेल काढून बोलण्याची पध्दत असते. हा भेद दाखविण्यासाठी विशिष्ट प्रकारची चिन्हही वापरली जातात. उदा. उच्च स्वरासाठी / आणि खालच्या आवाजासाठी \ अशी खूण केली जाते. मराठीत अजून असे चिन्ह वापरले जात नाही. बंजारा बोलीचा विचार केला तर मराठीच्याच अनुषंगाने विचार करीत असल्याकारणाने यातही असे चिन्ह वापरले जात नाही. मात्र आवाजाच्या चढउतारामुळे अर्थात बदल होतो. उदा. समजगो ( उच्च स्वरात ) - समजल का ? समजगो ( कमी स्वरात) - त्याला समजलं.
tone.locator: Chapter 2 (Banjara boli: svanim vichar), section 2.9 'बंजारा बोलीतील खंडाधिष्ठित स्वनिमांचे प्रकार' (types of suprasegmental phonemes), sub-head 'सुरावली (आरोह - अवरोह)', thesis p. 133 (section runs pp. 132-134)
tone.translation: In some languages there is a manner of speaking with a rise-fall (of pitch) or with a particular drawl. Special marks are also used to show this distinction, e.g. / for high pitch and \ for low voice. In Marathi no such mark is used as yet. Considering the Banjara dialect, since it is being treated along the lines of Marathi, no such mark is used in it either. However, a change of meaning does come about through the rise and fall of the voice, e.g. samajgo (in a high pitch) - 'understood?'; samajgo (in a low pitch) - 'he understood.'
tone.summary: Pitch (सुरावली / आरोह-अवरोह, 'intonation, rise-fall') is listed among the suprasegmental phonemes of Banjara (Labhani) boli but is described and exemplified only as utterance-level intonation distinguishing a question from a statement (samajgo high = 'understood?', samajgo low = 'he understood'); no lexical tone contrast, tone inventory or tone marking is given, i.e. no lexical tone.
